cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

cardFidelity.evidence: A5 adopts six matching plates and suppresses counting, combining some accommodation with concealment, but A1 and A3 authority remains weakly contextualized.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 flowers/plain mismatch causes A3 potatoes; B4 matching demand causes A5 five new plates.

relationship.evidence: B4 refuses camouflage and specifies the desired set; A follows that preference.

heightening.evidence: A5 expands one covert replacement into a whole visible matching set to avoid accounting for the old one.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard/Sunday lunch and B2 pattern provide understandable domestic stakes.
